title: Comparing Sales Data: A Small Café's Year
instructions: 阅读下面的短文，回答10个问题。短文和题目均为模拟材料，不是真实考试。请根据短文内容选择或填写答案。填空题答案必须与原文完全一致，且不超过字数限制。
passage:
Last year, a small café called 'The Corner Cup' compared its monthly sales. The owner, Maria, wanted to understand trends. She looked at data from January to December. In January, sales were low: only 200 cups of coffee were sold. In February, sales increased to 250 cups. March showed a slight decrease to 240 cups. April had a big jump to 350 cups. May was similar to April, with 360 cups. June sales dropped to 300 cups. July and August were the best months: 500 cups each. September fell to 400 cups. October had 380 cups. November rose to 450 cups. December reached 480 cups.

Maria also compared food sales. In January, 100 sandwiches were sold. February had 120. March was 110. April jumped to 200. May was 210. June dropped to 180. July and August were 300 each. September was 250. October was 240. November was 280. December was 290.

There was a clear trend: summer months had higher sales. There were more customers in July and August. The café was busier then. In winter, there were fewer customers. Maria noticed that coffee sales were always higher than sandwich sales. For example, in July, coffee sales were 500 cups, but sandwich sales were only 300. The difference was 200.

Maria also looked at the percentage of sales for each product. Coffee made up about 60% of total sales, and sandwiches made up about 40%. In summer, coffee was 65% and sandwiches 35%. In winter, coffee was 55% and sandwiches 45%. So, coffee was always more popular.

Maria decided to add more seats for summer. She also planned to offer a winter discount. She said, 'There was a big difference between summer and winter. We need to prepare for both.'

After reviewing the data, Maria made a chart. The chart showed coffee sales in blue and sandwich sales in orange. The blue bars were taller in every month. This helped her see the trend quickly. She also calculated the average monthly coffee sales. The average was about 370 cups. For sandwiches, the average was about 200. She compared these averages. Coffee sales were almost double sandwich sales.

Maria shared the chart with her staff. They discussed why summer was busier. One reason was the nice weather. People liked to sit outside. Another reason was the tourist season. Many visitors came to the town in July and August. In winter, the weather was cold, so fewer people went out. The café was quieter.

Maria also looked at the cost of ingredients. Coffee beans cost more in winter. The price increased by 10%. Sandwiches used bread and cheese. Their prices were stable. So, in winter, coffee was more expensive to make. But coffee was still more popular. Maria decided to keep the same prices for customers. She did not want to lose them.

Finally, Maria set a goal for next year. She wanted to increase coffee sales by 5% in winter. She planned to offer a warm coffee drink special. She also wanted to increase sandwich sales in summer by 10%. She would add new sandwich fillings. She believed these changes would help. The café would be busier all year.

Maria also compared the number of staff working each month. In January, there were only two staff members. In July and August, there were five staff members. In December, there were three staff members. She needed more staff in busy months. The staff cost was higher in summer. But the café earned more money then. Maria was happy with the data. She said, 'The numbers tell a clear story. We can plan better now.'

grammar.title: 比较结构；百分比与数量表达；there was / were；趋势动词
grammar.explanation: 比较结构用于比较两个事物，如 higher than, more popular。百分比用百分号表示，如60%。数量表达用数字加名词，如200 cups。there was/were 表示某处有某物，单数用was，复数用were。趋势动词描述变化，如increase, decrease, jump, drop。
grammar.example: Coffee sales were always higher than sandwich sales.

options: There was more customers in July.
There were more customers in July.
There were more customer in July.
There was more customer in July.
answers: There were more customers in July.
questions.evidence: There were more customers in July and August.

questions.prompt: Coffee sales were 500 cups. Sandwich sales were 300. Coffee sales were ______ than sandwich sales.
questions.evidence: coffee sales were always higher than sandwich sales.

questions.prompt: In summer, coffee was 65% and sandwiches 35%. So coffee was ______ popular.

questions.evidence: In February, sales increased to 250 cups.
